title: Linux patches can take weeks, and OpenAI and Cisco built Shirudo to help in the meantime
summary: OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, an open-source tool that puts temporary protections on running Linux systems while their owners work on a patch. Shirudo is Japanese for “shield,” which is also what each protection is called: a small program that blocks the specific behavior a vulnerability depends on, with no restart needed.
